title: Metal Slug 3
subtitle: A campaign with more than one route
summary: Metal Slug 3 is SNK's run-and-gun adventure, first released for Neo Geo MVS in Japan on 23 March 2000.
body: Metal Slug 3 is SNK's run-and-gun adventure, first released for Neo Geo MVS in Japan on 23 March 2000. The four-member squad returns to confront Morden's remaining forces and a renewed alien threat. Infantry shooting, rescued prisoners and powerful vehicles connect stages filled with extravagant creatures and machinery. Branching paths are its major addition, allowing a mission to lead through different hazards before rejoining at the boss. The choice gives repeated attempts another purpose: a familiar opening may now carry the player into a different stretch of the campaign.

Alternative routes can vary in length and difficulty, offering different equipment and opportunities to rescue prisoners. Choosing one therefore changes more than the scenery. A useful vehicle or weapon can affect how the next encounter is approached, while surviving preserves the score value of the people rescued along the way. Close attacks, grenades and found firearms remain the squad's basic tools. The branches make those familiar tools serve another sequence of problems, encouraging players to learn several ways through a mission rather than memorise a single uninterrupted path.

The campaign steadily increases the scale of its confrontations, moving from recognisable military enemies towards alien machinery and an extended final operation. Detailed animation keeps ordinary soldiers and small comic reactions visible inside the spectacle. The music includes work by Masato Horiuchi, Takushi Hiyamuta and Yoshihiko Wada. Metal Slug 3 draws its variety from the relationship between its simple controls and the situations built around them: another vehicle, transformation or route can change the immediate task while the player continues to run, jump and fire through the action.
